examples.title: Valid program
examples.description: Functions, a while loop and arithmetic. Parses cleanly; shows the token stream and AST.
examples.why: Baseline: what a correct program looks like through every stage.

examples.title: Missing semicolon
examples.description: A declaration without its ';'. Bison only notices at the next line.
examples.why: The detection point (next line) differs from the cause; layout evidence locates the line end.

examples.title: Missing ')'
examples.description: An if-condition without its closing parenthesis.
examples.why: One clearly best repair; alternatives exist but need follow-on edits.

examples.title: Missing '{'
examples.description: A while loop whose body lost its opening brace; the error surfaces lines later.
examples.why: Structurally different repairs parse; indentation evidence ranks the intended one first, but the margin is small so IntelliFix reports alternatives.

examples.title: Missing operand
examples.description: A binary operator without its right operand.
examples.why: Deleting the operator or inventing an operand are both possible; IntelliFix does not pretend to know which.

examples.title: Two errors
examples.description: A missing ';' and a missing ')' in the same function.
examples.why: Hypothesis lanes repair the errors one after another and test which later diagnostics are stable.

examples.title: Ambiguous operator
examples.description: Two operands with no operator between them.
examples.why: Many structurally different repairs are equally supported: a textbook case for abstention.

examples.title: Missing variable name
examples.why: Every repair must invent an identifier, so IntelliFix reports low confidence instead of guessing.

examples.title: Valid nested program
examples.description: Arrays, for-loops, nested if/else and logical operators.
examples.why: Shows a deeper AST and the lack of false alarms on valid code.

examples.title: Invalid character
examples.why: Lexical error tokens flow into the parser; deleting vs. replacing the character changes the AST.

examples.title: Unsupported C construct
examples.description: Uses i++, which MiniC deliberately omits.
examples.why: IntelliFix distinguishes 'not MiniC' from a typo and refuses to silently rewrite it.

examples.title: Extra ')'
examples.description: A duplicated closing parenthesis after a call.
examples.why: Deleting the extra ')' and inserting a matching '(' produce the same AST and are grouped; the runner-up (turning ')' into ';', i.e. an extra empty statement) is structurally different, and the margin (1.0) is below the dev-selected threshold, so IntelliFix lists alternatives while ranking the intended repair first.

note: Bundled sample programs; all outputs are computed live by the compiler.
